ties.applies_to: U.S. senator and U.S. representative: no person receives a plurality of the votes cast in the state or in either congressional district (R.I. Gen. Laws 17-4-7)
ties.steps: a new election is held in the state or the district on the fourth Tuesday after the election at which there was no choice; new certificates of nomination or nomination papers are filed ten days before it
ties.who: the voters, at a new election

sources.quote: In case no person receives a plurality of the votes cast in the state or in either congressional district at any election, a new election shall be held in the state or in the district on the fourth (4th) Tuesday after the holding of the election at which there was no choice.

ties.note: The section does not use the word tie; a tie for the most votes is read as 'no person receives a plurality' [inferred]. 17-4-6 says the person receiving the largest number of votes is declared elected.

ties.applies_to: the general offices of governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general and general treasurer: failure of any person to receive a plurality (R.I. Gen. Laws 17-2-3)
ties.steps: on a failure to elect one of these officers the general assembly, on its organization, meets in grand committee and elects someone to fill the office; where the failure is that no person received a plurality, the election is made from the persons who received the same and largest number of votes; the person receiving a majority of the votes in the grand committee is elected
ties.who: the general assembly in grand committee

sources.quote: When the general assembly elects any of the officers because of the failure of any person to receive a plurality of the votes cast, the election in each case shall be made from the persons who received the same and largest number of votes.
In elections by the general assembly in grand committee, the person receiving a majority of the votes shall be elected.

ties.note: The Rhode Island Constitution was not read.

ties.applies_to: senator or representative in the general assembly: no election made in a district (R.I. Gen. Laws 17-3-3)
ties.steps: the state board notifies the secretary of state of the failure to elect; the secretary of state directs the local boards to issue warrants for the election to proceed on the tenth day from the date of the warrant (next non-holiday day if a holiday, never Saturday) for the officer for which there was no choice, on a ballot with the names of the candidates for that office
ties.who: the voters of the district, at an adjourned election

sources.quote: If it appears by the count of the state board that no election has been made of any one or more of the senators or representatives in the general assembly, at any election held for those officers, the board shall, immediately after the count, notify the secretary of state of the failure to elect; the secretary of state shall, immediately after the notification, direct the local boards in the senatorial or representative districts to issue their warrants to the moderators of the district, districts, or voting districts, as the case may be, directing the election to proceed on the tenth (10th) day from the date of the warrant

ties.note: The section does not use the word tie; a tie for the most votes is read as 'no election has been made' [inferred]. The section does not say whether a recount comes first. The Rhode Island Constitution was not read.

ties.applies_to: a failure to make a nomination or to elect a candidate to party office at a primary by reason of a tie vote (R.I. Gen. Laws 17-15-33)
ties.steps: the vacancy is filled by the party committee: the executive committee of the state committee for an office filled by the voters of more than one city or town (the senatorial or representative district committee for a senatorial or representative committee), or the city or town committee for an office filled by the voters of no more than one city or town; the choice is only of one of the candidates receiving the tie vote, and the name is certified to the state or local board
ties.who: the executive committee of the state committee, the district committee, or the city or town committee of the party

sources.quote: If there is a failure to make a nomination or to elect a candidate to party office at any primary by reason of a tie vote, the vacancy, if in respect to an office to be filled by the voters of more than one city or town, shall be filled by the executive committee of the state committee of the respective party
The vacancy shall be filled only by the choice of one of the candidates receiving the tie vote.

ties.steps: 17-4-10 says the candidates having a plurality of the legal votes are elected; no provision found saying what a tie does
ties.note: Read: R.I. Gen. Laws 17-4-6, 17-4-7, 17-4-10, 17-22-5, 17-22-6. 17-4-7 (new election when no person receives a plurality 'in the state') might be read to reach a tied slate of electors, but it speaks of senators and representatives in the sections around it; not decided. An absence cannot be confirmed from these sections.

ties.steps: no provision found saying what a tie in a local election does
ties.note: Read in Title 17: 17-19-34, 17-19-36 (local returns and certificates), 17-8 index (local canvassing authorities), 17-15-33 (primary tie, party offices). A tie in a town or city election is probably governed by municipal charters, which were not read (state general law only).

ties.applies_to: a proposed amendment of the Constitution or a question submitted to the electors of the state (R.I. Gen. Laws 17-5-6)
ties.steps: 17-5-6 says the state board counts the votes and declares the result; no provision found saying what a tie does
ties.note: Read: 17-5-6 and 17-5 index; the Rhode Island Constitution (which sets the majority needed to adopt an amendment) was not read.

threshold.percent_of: the number of votes cast in the race (including irregular ballots, 17-19-37.1(1)(b))
threshold.conditions: races in which a single candidate is elected; 20,000 or fewer votes cast; recount by manual re-feeding of the computer ballots into the optical scan equipment; petition to the state board within nine days (local boards, 17-19-36) or seven days (state declaration, 17-19-37)
threshold.in_words: a trailing candidate may request a recount if trailing by less than 2% or 200 votes, whichever is less, where 20,000 or fewer votes are cast

who_may_request: a candidate for election or nomination for election to public office who trails the winning candidate
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in this section; the notice of a primary recount hearing is served at the petitioner's expense (17-15-35(a))

sources.quote: In those races where the number of votes cast is less than or equal to twenty thousand (20,000) the candidate requesting the recount shall trail the winning candidate by two percent (2%) or two hundred (200) votes, whichever is less;

recounts.note: Applies to races in which a single candidate is elected: 'a candidate who trails the winning candidate may request a recount ... provided that the candidate shall trail the winning candidate by less than the following number of votes'. The deadline to petition the state board is nine days after the election for a local declaration (17-19-36) and seven days after the state board's declaration (17-19-37). Kinds are a mapping of 'public office' (including nomination) [inferred]. A tie is not described: no candidate 'trails the winning candidate' where there is no winner.

threshold.percent_of: the number of votes cast in the race
threshold.conditions: a candidate who trails by 5% or less but by more than the minimum percentage or number of votes in the tiers above may petition the state board for a recount by re-reading the programmed memory devices and comparing with the election-night totals; if after that recount the candidate trails by less than the tier's number the candidate may request the manual re-feeding recount
threshold.in_words: a candidate trailing by five percent or less may petition for a re-reading of the memory devices of each precinct (a lesser recount); if that leaves the candidate within the tier thresholds, the full re-feeding recount may be requested

recounts.note: A machine-memory check, not a count of ballots, up to a 5% margin.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast in the race
threshold.conditions: the write-in candidate must have received a minimum of ten votes or one percent of the votes cast, whichever is greater, after the initial manual count of irregular ballots (at least ten votes where only write-in candidates receive votes), and must trail the winning candidate by less than the number required under 17-19-37.1(1) or (2); the recount is a manual recount of the irregular ballots
threshold.in_words: a write-in candidate with at least ten votes or one percent of the votes cast (whichever is greater) who also trails by less than the margin required for a recount under 17-19-37.1

sources.quote: A write-in candidate for election to public office shall be eligible to request a recount of the votes cast in a race: (a) If, following the initial manual count of all irregular ballots, the write-in candidate shall have received a minimum of ten (10) votes or one percent (1%) of the votes cast in the race, whichever is greater;

recounts.note: The numbers 10 and 1% are the eligibility floor for the write-in candidate's own votes, not the margin; the margin is the tiered margin of 17-19-37.1.

unread.what: the Rhode Island Constitution, city and town charters and Title 45 (towns and cities), and any rule of the state board of elections on recount cost
unread.reason: not read: state general law only for local offices; the Constitution was not fetched; the recount-cost provisions were not found in the Title 17 sections read

notes: Read, section by section, from the General Assembly's site: chapters 17-2, 17-3, 17-4, 17-5, 17-15 and 17-19 (recount eligibility 17-19-37.1 to 37.3), 17-22 (index plus 17-22-5 and 17-22-6), 17-8 and 17-1 (index only).

Rhode Island has no automatic recount and no recount on a tie in the sections read: every recount is requested by a trailing candidate (or, for questions, a person of recognized standing) within a size-tiered margin, and a tie leaves 'no plurality' (new election for Congress and the general assembly), a vote of the general assembly (general offices), or a party committee (primaries).
